topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, connecting previous practical histopathology work to the lecture's learning outcomes on cellular transformation, genetics, and cancer development.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to evaluate cellular transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, Tumor Suppressor Genes, and Genetic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the definitions, cell-cycle checkpoint pathways, and distinct genetic modes of action that characterize oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Cellular Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair mechanisms, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumor Progression, Hereditary Predisposition, and Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how the stepwise accumulation of inherited and acquired mutations drives tumor development, clinical predisposition syndromes, and tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, wrapping up the lecture with suggested reading and a preview of the upcoming session.
